subject: Packaging shapefiles for download in a shiny server app

messages.author: d16ad2363b1378ab
messages.subject: Packaging shapefiles for download in a shiny server app
parts:
Hi -

New to shiny, and I'm developing an app that would one day be hosted on a server.  I have functionality that allows users to download shapefiles that are created by their interactions in the app.  While I've been testing, I've been using writeOGR to write shapefiles to a directory within the app directory, zip them up, and offer them up for download, but I'm wondering if this would cause problems with multiple users.  In a server setting with multiple users, would these files be written to session-specific sub-directories, or would they all go into the same directory?  Are you even allowed to write files in this way?

I haven't been able to find a way to transform a Spatial*DataFrame to a shapefile and store it in a variable of some sort to then pass to the downloadHandler.

Thanks for any pointers.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Packaging shapefiles for download in a shiny server app
parts: The most obvious way is to do the actual writing of the shapefiles directly in the downloadHandler (or from a function you call from the downloadHandler). That way you don't have to think about where files are stored at all.

messages.subject: Re: Packaging shapefiles for download in a shiny server app
parts:
Righto - it certainly works as a standalone app (I already had the writing, zipping, and cleaning up occurring inside the downloadHandler).  I'll test it out when it comes time to upload to a server.  It's really just a matter of knowing how careful and precise I need to be with certain commands, e.g. zip all files in a directory vs. looking for specific filenames.  Since there's a default name for the files to be zipped (changeable by the user), I'm just concerned that if/when multiple users are active, that one might unexpectedly download some other user's shapefiles.  I suppose since the writing, zipping, and deleting occurs quickly, the chances are slim even if every user's downloadHandler is looking at the same directory.  (Some of my confusion results simply from a lack of understanding of how apps function in a server setting.)

Joe - truly amazing work this is.  As an avid R user and advocate, it was great to discover shiny.  I think it'll really help prove R's (and shiny's!) potential value to our organization.
